research_rationale: Executive Order 10129 (15 FR 3499 (Federal Register of June 6, 1950)) was signed June 3, 1950. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date; the text breaks across a page after paragraph 7 and resumes on a later page of the same issue, so paragraph 7 appears in two pieces. It creates the President's Commission on Migratory Labor (paragraph 1), directs it to inquire into five subjects (paragraph 2), requires a written report by December 15, 1950 (paragraph 3), authorizes hearings (paragraph 4), directs consultation with the Department of State (paragraph 5), directs agency cooperation (paragraph 6), provides funding for the fiscal years 1950 and 1951 from the Emergency Fund for the President (paragraph 7) and provides in paragraph 8 that the Commission ceases to exist thirty days after its report unless otherwise determined by further Executive Order. On 2026-10-14 every clause is terminated on May 31, 1951, the day the Commission ceased to exist. Executive Order 10192 (15 FR 9029 (Federal Register of December 19, 1950)), signed December 15, 1950, amended paragraph 3 (the report date becomes March 1, 1951) and paragraph 8 (“Thirty days” becomes “Sixty days”). Executive Order 10236 (16 FR 3607 (Federal Register of April 27, 1951)), signed April 26, 1951, amended paragraph 8 as amended to read “The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31,1951.”, which fixes the end. The report date of paragraph 3 and the report-relative cessation of paragraph 8 are not ends: the held corpus does not give the date the report was rendered, and Executive Order 10236 replaced the report-relative rule with a fixed date while the Commission still existed. Executive Order 10193's Federal Register page contains the text of Executive Order 10192 and cites Executive Order 10129 only for that reason; it is not a separate amendment. The held-text search for citations of the order found only Executive Orders 10192, 10236 and their page copies. The Federal Register disposition-note search lists two hits (the 10192 and 10236 amendments); the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit.
savings_reason: The order's text has no saving clause. The Commission's report and recommendations were produced during its life and are not commands of the order; the bounded searches found no later order that continues or revives the Commission.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end is shown. The held corpus does not state when the report was rendered, but Executive Order 10236 of April 26, 1951 amended paragraph 8 to a fixed date and treats the Commission as continuing to May 31, 1951; had the report-relative period already run, there would have been nothing left to amend. The date recorded is May 31, 1951; Executive Order 10236 says the Commission ceases “at the end of” that day, so the inclusive and exclusive readings coincide with the close of May 31, 1951. A report deadline is not an end, and the amendments are later events.
